summary: No reachable vulnerabilities. history.state is a structured clone (no getters/proxies), so entryKey() only does a typeof check and a property read; null, primitives and foreign objects fall through safely. The new step-off rule calls history.back() only when the popped state's key equals lastTableKey, a 128-bit crypto.getRandomValues value a different same-origin page cannot guess. Even a crafted chain of entries carrying that key (devtools only) makes each back() land one entry further back, so it ends at the first non-matching entry or the start of the session history. It cannot loop forever and there is no forward re-entry. The CSPRNG key is used for uniqueness only and is not a secret. e2e/support/hold-writes.ts, which patches IDBDatabase.prototype.transaction, is imported only by e2e/pause-history.spec.ts and loaded through page.addInitScript. Nothing in src/ or index.html imports it, and the current dist/ has no __tlhSessionsHold marker, so it cannot ship. No new dependencies.
